record.original_question: Do polynomial-time algorithms exist to decide whether a given embedded graph has a large-edge-width weight function, and whether a given graph has some embedding with a large-edge-width weight function?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.4 Do there exist polynomial-time algorithms for the following questions? • Given an embedded graph G, does G have an LEW-weight function? • Does a given graph G have an embedding with an LEW-weight function?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite graph 2-cell embedded in a closed surface. A weight function on G is an assignment w: E(G) → ℝ_{>0} of positive real numbers to edges. For a closed walk C in G, let w(C) denote the sum of the weights of the edges traversed by C (with multiplicity). The weight function w is called a large-edge-width (LEW) weight function if, for every non-contractible closed walk C in the embedded graph G and every facial walk F, one has w(C) > w(F).

Decide the following:

(a) Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm which, given an embedded graph G, determines whether G admits an LEW-weight function?

(b) Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm which, given an abstract graph G, determines whether G has some 2-cell embedding (in some closed surface) that admits an LEW-weight function?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for polynomial-time algorithms recognizing LEW-weight functions on embedded graphs did not return any source that decisively resolves either question. Related work exists on computing the (unweighted) edge-width of embedded graphs, but no published result was found confirming or refuting the existence of polynomial-time algorithms for the LEW-weight recognition problems.
